title: Alphabet Inverted Triangle Pattern
statement:
Write a function to generate an alphabet inverted triangle pattern of height `n`.

Row `i` (0-indexed, from `0` to `n - 1`) should contain letters starting from `A` up to the `n - i`-th letter of the alphabet (where A is index 1, B is 2, etc. - e.g. for row 0 it is from A to `n`-th letter) concatenated without spaces.

The rows should be separated by newline characters (`\n`). There should be no trailing spaces in any row, and no trailing newline at the end of the final row.

For example, if `n = 4`, the output should be:
```
ABCD
ABC
AB
A
```

editorial.approach: Run an outer loop `i` from `0` to `n - 1`. For each row `i`, build a string by appending characters from code 65 (`A`) to `65 + (n - 1 - i)`. Join rows with `\n`.

hints: The first row has letters from A to the `n`-th letter of the alphabet.
Row `i` (0-indexed) has letters from A up to `65 + n - 1 - i`.
Slice a precomputed string of the alphabet to do this efficiently.

bruteForceSolution.explanation: Iterate `i` from `0` to `n-1`. For each row, run an inner loop `j` from `0` to `n - 1 - i` and append the corresponding letter.

optimizedSolution.explanation: Precompute the alphabet sequence up to `n`, then take slices of decreasing lengths (`0` to `n - i`) to construct the rows.

interviewExplanation: An inverted letter triangle prints prefixes of the alphabet with decreasing lengths. We construct the full sequence of length `n` once, then extract slices of size `n - i` for each row, optimizing construction.
